problem: Humans learn efficiently by combining linguistic guidance from others with direct experience, but how to formally model and implement this social learning remains unclear.
approach: A computational framework that treats social learning as joint probabilistic inference over executable world models, using a language model to model how humans share advice and enabling agents to interpret language as evidence in Bayesian inference.
contribution: Demonstrated through behavioral experiments and simulations across 10 video games that linguistic guidance reduces risky interactions and speeds discovery; showed successful knowledge transfer between humans and models through iterated learning.

problem: Self-supervised learning requires long pretraining to learn good representations, but the optimal pretraining duration is unclear and longer training does not always improve generalization.
approach: Frames SSL learning phases through critical periods by injecting data deficits and measuring representation quality via downstream tasks; uses Fisher Information on pretext objectives to estimate network plasticity during pretraining.
contribution: Identified that SSL models exhibit critical periods where intermediate checkpoints yield stronger out-of-domain generalization, while longer pretraining primarily benefits in-domain accuracy.

problem: Text clustering typically produces numeric centroids that are not interpretable or auditable, and LLM-based clustering methods are expensive.
approach: Replaces numeric k-means centroids with textual summaries; proposes k-NLPmeans using lightweight deterministic summarizers and k-LLMmeans using LLMs under a fixed budget that does not grow with dataset size.
contribution: Consistently outperforms classical baselines and approaches LLM-based clustering accuracy without extensive LLM calls; provides a StackExchange-derived benchmark for streaming text clustering.

problem: Actor-critic algorithms are widely used in deep RL but their finite-time convergence with deep neural network approximation in continuous spaces remains largely unexplored.
approach: Provides finite-time analysis of single-timescale actor-critic with deep neural network approximation by simultaneously controlling reward error, critic error, and actor error in the time-average reward setting.
contribution: Establishes convergence to a stationary point at rate O(T^{-1/2}) and validates theoretical guarantees on MuJoCo benchmarks.

problem: Single-molecule localization microscopy requires non-overlapping fluorophores for accurate reconstruction, limiting live-cell imaging; existing deep learning approaches rely on non-differentiable NMS layers that discard true positives.
approach: Reformulates SMLM training as a set-matching problem with optimal transport loss eliminating NMS during inference; proposes iterative neural network that integrates optical system knowledge.
contribution: Surpasses state-of-the-art at moderate and high emitter densities on synthetic and real biological data.

problem: Vision-language models as zero-shot value functions have limited generalization and cannot effectively reason over temporal sequences.
approach: Introduces VITA, which enhances VLMs through test-time adaptation via a lightweight module updated on meta-learned self-supervised loss; uses dissimilarity-based sampling to prevent shortcut learning.
contribution: Generalizes from single training environment to diverse out-of-distribution tasks, environments, and embodiments; value estimates enable reward shaping in offline RL with Meta-World performance exceeding fuzzy-logic rewards.

problem: Transformers must independently encode positional and symbolic information, but how Rotary Position Encodings achieve this dichotomy is not well understood.
approach: Formalizes positional versus symbolic head behaviors with quantitative metrics; analyzes how RoPE encodes information via frequency components and demonstrates causal control over model performance via frequency access.
contribution: Shows strong correspondence between attention head behavior and frequency use; demonstrates that controlling which frequencies heads access directly controls Transformer performance.

problem: Diffusion transformers require expensive multi-step inference; token caching methods fail to achieve superior acceleration in few-step models due to inefficient strategies and complete forward computations.
approach: Proposes differentiable layer-wise sparsity optimization via learnable network and dynamic programming solver; eliminates need for full-step processing through two-stage training.
contribution: Achieves 54% computational cost reduction on PixArt-α with 20 steps while surpassing original model's generation metrics; outperforms prior approaches across DiT, PixArt, FLUX, Wan2.1.

problem: Differentially private deep transfer learning requires choosing clipping bound and batch size, but theory-practice mismatch exists and existing heuristics fail under strong privacy constraints.
approach: Analyzes gradient distribution changes under privacy and shows that cumulative DP noise better explains batch size performance than existing heuristics; frames clipping as gradient re-weighting.
contribution: Identifies that single (C,B) settings across tasks lead to suboptimal performance; explains when performance drops occur between loose/tight privacy and plentiful/limited compute settings.

problem: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards for LLMs relies on path-based metrics that ignore reasoning tree structures, limiting data efficiency.
approach: Introduces Reasoning Score (r-score) measuring query learning difficulty from reasoning tree structure; proposes Reasoning Tree Schedule (Re-Schedule) curriculum progressing from structurally simple to complex queries.
contribution: Achieves up to 3.2% accuracy gains on six math-reasoning benchmarks using structural understanding of reasoning trees.

problem: Causal discovery under interventions with latent confounding is theoretically underexplored; understanding false-negative rates on realistic graph structures is unclear.
approach: Analyzes false-negative rate concentration for sparse Erdős-Rényi and Barabási-Albert graphs under single-variable interventions with ε-interventional faithfulness.
contribution: Shows FNR concentrates at rate O(log d / sqrt(d)) for ER graphs; demonstrates FNR deviation vanishes for BA graphs with degree exponent γ > 3, indicating heterogeneous networks intrinsically regularize causal discovery.

problem: Logarithmic post-training quantization is hardware-efficient but limited by nonlinear symmetric grids and standard rounding, causing accuracy loss.
approach: Introduces learnable Logarithmic Adaptive Rounding Techniques (LogART) with task-aware rounding; extends to outlier-aware asymmetric and hardware-friendly dynamic bases via distribution-aware search.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on various architectures and ultra-low bitwidths; outperforms existing logarithmic PTQ methods while maintaining efficiency.

problem: Evaluating multimodal LLMs remains incomplete; current benchmarks do not comprehensively assess spatial reasoning, commonsense knowledge, and environment interaction in real-world scenarios.
approach: Introduces SpaCE-Eval, a visual-question-answering benchmark with human-produced diagrams testing spatial reasoning, commonsense physics, and environmental interaction through diagram-question pairs refined via rigorous pipeline.
contribution: Demonstrates that leading MLLMs significantly underperform on spatial reasoning, indicating substantial enhancement necessary for real-world environmental understanding.

problem: LLM-as-a-Judge for evaluation is costly and opaque; using small models for evaluation has been dismissed due to weak generative ability.
approach: Proposes Representation-as-a-Judge paradigm that probes small model hidden states instead of prompted output; introduces INSPECTOR framework predicting aspect-level scores from internal representations.
contribution: INSPECTOR substantially outperforms prompting-based small LMs and closely approximates full LLM judges on reasoning benchmarks while offering efficiency, reliability, and interpretability.

problem: Generating complete code repositories from scratch remains fundamentally challenging despite LLM capabilities in individual functions.
approach: Introduces Repository Planning Graph (RPG) encoding capabilities, file structures, data flows, and functions in unified graph; develops ZeroRepo with proposal-level planning, implementation construction, and graph-guided code generation.
contribution: On RepoCraft benchmark, produces 3.9x larger code than strongest baseline with 81.5% coverage and 69.7% test accuracy; generates approximately 36K Code Lines and 445K Code Tokens.

problem: Video class-incremental learning must prevent catastrophic forgetting while capturing spatiotemporal structures without memory-intensive exemplar rehearsal.
approach: Proposes Spatiotemporal Preservation and Routing (StPR) with Frame-Shared Semantics Distillation identifying stable channels and Temporal Decomposition Mixture-of-Experts routing task-specific experts by temporal dynamics.
contribution: Achieves exemplar-free VCIL by preserving spatial semantics and temporal dynamics without requiring task IDs or stored exemplars.

problem: The mechanism by which in-context learning (ICL) works remains unclear; zero-shot performance is poor despite language models encoding relevant information.
approach: Demonstrates that LMs encode non-selective representations in zero-shot containing task-agnostic information; shows selective information removal via low-rank filters steers models to intended tasks, and ICL simulates this process.
contribution: Identifies Denoising Heads enabling task-oriented information removal; ablation experiments blocking removal operation show ICL accuracy degrades significantly, confirming the critical role of information removal.

problem: Video relighting faces trade-offs between lighting fidelity and temporal consistency; joint camera and illumination control for generative video rendering is underexplored.
approach: Proposes Light-X with disentangled design decoupling geometry via dynamic point clouds and lighting via relit frames; introduces Light-Syn degradation pipeline synthesizing multi-view multi-illumination training pairs from monocular footage.
contribution: Outperforms baseline methods in joint camera-illumination control; surpasses prior video relighting in text and background-conditioned settings.

problem: Finite-time convergence analysis for ODE-based generative models in stochastic interpolants framework remains largely unexplored despite their importance.
approach: Provides rigorous finite-time convergence analysis of numerical ODE implementations for stochastic interpolants; establishes discrete-time error bounds for forward Euler and Heun methods with optimized step size schedules.
contribution: Yields improved theoretical guarantees for diffusion models in terms of smoothness requirements and dimensional dependence; numerical experiments validate error bounds and complexity analyses.

problem: LLMs' pattern-matching abilities support in-distribution performance but limit compositional generalization; mechanisms of pattern matching and its failure modes are unclear.
approach: Formalizes pattern matching as functional equivalence identifying input subsequences with identical results; studies Transformer and Mamba on controlled compositional tasks isolating this mechanism.
contribution: Demonstrates instance-wise pattern matching success predicted by contexts witnessing functional equivalence; proves tight sample complexity bound for two-hop structures; identifies path ambiguity as structural barrier to unified representations.

problem: Score matching is central to diffusion models but its optimization behavior in over-parameterized regimes remains theoretically limited.
approach: Studies gradient descent for training over-parameterized models to learn single Gaussian; analyzes optimization under multiple noise-scale regimes with focus on convergence conditions and initialization effects.
contribution: Proves global convergence at sufficient noise scale resembling gradient EM behavior; identifies convergence under exponentially small initialization in low-noise regime and demonstrates failure cases without proper initialization.

problem: Image quality assessment typically focuses on whole-image analysis without capturing region-level structural degradation information.
approach: Introduces Distortion Graph (DG) representing image pairs as structured topology grounded in regions; proposes PandaSet dataset with region-level annotations and PandaBench suite evaluating region-level understanding.
contribution: Demonstrates that state-of-the-art MLLMs fail to understand region-level degradations; shows training on PandaSet or prompting with DG elicits region-wise distortion understanding.

problem: EEG-based motor imagery BCIs suffer from cross-subject and cross-session variability; existing test-time adaptation methods rely on expensive gradient-based fine-tuning or fail to capture temporal shifts.
approach: Proposes BTTA-DG using gradient-free Bayesian test-time adaptation; employs Dirichlet feature projection mapping temporal embeddings to compact parameter space and GMM-driven inference fusing historical evidence with model priors.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art EEG-TTA accuracy while running in real-time; significantly outperforms previous EEG-TTA methods.

problem: Data selection for LLM pretraining via perplexity-based filtering is computationally expensive and unreliable for noisy out-of-distribution samples.
approach: Proposes prior-based filtering estimating token priors via corpus-level term frequency statistics without model inference; filters documents by mean and standard deviation of token priors.
contribution: Achieves highest average performance across 20 downstream benchmarks while reducing time cost by over 1000x compared to perplexity filtering; applies to code and math without supervision.

problem: Real-time image segmentation on edge devices faces tight accuracy, latency, and energy budgets; extreme quantization degrades accuracy and lacks efficient GPU implementations.
approach: Introduces Masked Binary U-Net (MBU-Net) with cost-aware masking prioritizing where masking yields highest accuracy-per-cost; develops GPU framework mapping MBU-Net to Tensor Cores via bit-encoding.
contribution: Attains near full-precision accuracy on segmentation benchmarks while achieving near-binary efficiency on widely available GPUs.

problem: Existing multimodal browsing benchmarks do not require genuine multimodal reasoning; many tasks solvable with text-only heuristics.
approach: Introduces MMSearch-Plus benchmark with 311 tasks enforcing multimodal understanding via extraction and propagation of fine-grained visual cues through iterative retrieval; provides set-of-mark module for agent framework.
contribution: Strongest system achieves 36.0% end-to-end accuracy; SoM integration improves robustness with gains up to 3.9 points; reveals recurring errors in webpage location and visual similarity distinction.

problem: LLMs produce inconsistent output quality in complex reasoning tasks; identifying trustworthy responses remains difficult without reliability assessment.
approach: Proposes TokUR framework estimating token-level uncertainty via low-rank random weight perturbation during decoding; aggregates uncertainty to capture semantic uncertainty of responses.
contribution: Token-level uncertainty strongly correlates with answer correctness and model robustness; uncertainty signals enhance mathematical reasoning performance at test time.

problem: When predictive models anticipate undesired future events, determining which variables can be altered to avoid outcomes remains unclear.
approach: Introduces framework evaluating actionable variable influence on avoiding undesired futures via maximum expected utility principle; quantifies influence beyond statistical correlation.
contribution: Reveals counterintuitive insight that influential variables may not have intrinsically strong causal effects; demonstrates utility of altering weak causal factors or non-intrinsic variables.

problem: Current LLM safety alignment imposes universal standards failing to account for individual sensitivities to content.
approach: Proposes training-free inference-time personalized safety control via activation intervention; evaluates three strategies for estimating intervention directions with focus on Paired Contrast Mean Shift (PCMS).
contribution: Effectively reduces undesired content per individual preferences with minimal impact on helpfulness across diverse open-weight models.

problem: Retrieval-augmented generation struggles with ineffective task decomposition and redundant retrieval introducing noise; reasoning with external knowledge remains challenging.
approach: Proposes DeepRAG modeling retrieval-augmented reasoning as Markov Decision Process; iteratively decomposes queries and dynamically determines when to retrieve versus rely on parametric reasoning.
contribution: Improves retrieval efficiency and boosts answer accuracy by 25.41%.

problem: Mathematical reasoning in video requires interpreting fine-grained visual information, reading text, and integrating spoken cues over extended time; existing benchmarks lack this complexity.
approach: Introduces VideoMathQA benchmark with 920 man-hours of expert annotation spanning 10 mathematical domains and 10-second to 1-hour videos; includes multi-step reasoning annotations for fine-grained diagnosis.
contribution: Establishes evaluation framework for temporally extended cross-modal mathematical reasoning; demonstrates significant challenge for MLLMs including closed and open-source models.

problem: Machine unlearning methods suffer from catastrophic forgetting and metric imbalance; small perturbations can be exploited by relearn and jailbreak attacks.
approach: Proposes PRISM enforcing dual-space smoothness in representation and parameter spaces; includes representation-space robustness via probes and parameter-space decoupling of gradient conflicts.
contribution: Outperforms SOTA baselines under multiple attacks while achieving better balance among metrics on conversational and continuous-text settings.

problem: The k-hyperplane clustering problem (minimizing sum of squared distances to k hyperplanes) is NP-hard and global optimization remains challenging.
approach: Solves k-HC2 via spatial branch-and-bound by strengthening mixed integer quadratically-constrained formulation with constraints from p-norm variants; focuses on polyhedral norms.
contribution: Achieves speedups from 41 to 1.5 orders of magnitude, drastically improving solvability to global optimality.

problem: Existing model editing techniques degrade in massive editing scenarios; embedding misalignment among knowledge items undermines editing reliability at scale.
approach: Proposes EAMET addressing embedding misalignment by aligning key and residual embedding space; enables massive editing while maintaining robustness in context-rich settings.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing methods achieving approximately 90% editing efficacy when editing 10k facts.

problem: Extending online reinforcement learning to diffusion models is challenging due to intractable likelihoods; existing methods have solver restrictions, forward-reverse inconsistency, and CFG integration issues.
approach: Introduces DiffusionNFT optimizing diffusion models via flow matching on forward process; contrasts positive and negative generations defining implicit policy improvement naturally incorporating reinforcement signals.
contribution: Up to 25x more efficient than FlowGRPO; improves GenEval from 0.24 to 0.98 within 1k steps; significantly boosts SD3.5-Medium performance on every benchmark.

problem: Explaining neural network decisions at scale remains challenging; existing explainability methods do not scale well while reducing explanation size.
approach: Proposes FAME (Formal Abstract Minimal Explanations) grounded in abstract interpretation; designs dedicated perturbation domains eliminating traversal order need and leverages LiRPA bounds to discard irrelevant features.
contribution: Consistent gains in explanation size and runtime on medium to large-scale networks compared to VERIX+; introduces procedure measuring worst-case distance to true minimal explanations.

problem: LLM evaluation focuses on single-turn fully-specified instructions; multi-turn conversational performance remains underexplored despite frequent underspecification in user instructions.
approach: Performs large-scale simulations comparing LLM performance in single and multi-turn settings; decomposes performance degradation into aptitude loss and reliability increase.
contribution: All tested top LLMs show average 39% performance drop in multi-turn conversations; discovers that when LLMs take a wrong turn, they get lost and fail to recover.

problem: Pre-trained language models are vulnerable to backdoor attacks via trigger patterns in training data; existing defenses are limited.
approach: Investigates internal behavior shifts in backdoored models focusing on attention and gradient attribution when processing poisoned inputs; proposes inference-time defense combining token-level attention and gradient anomaly scores.
contribution: Significantly reduces attack success rates compared to baselines; provides interpretability-driven analysis of scoring mechanism for trigger localization and defense robustness.

problem: Chain-of-Thought training advances LLM reasoning but mechanisms enabling compositional generalization remain inadequately understood.
approach: Demonstrates models combine learned skills during CoT training; formalizes compositional generalization through information-theoretic bounds decomposed into ID and OOD components; analyzes two-stage compositional circuit structure.
contribution: Theoretically proves CoT achieves generalization by composing skills; structurally shows CoT creates two-stage circuits where intermediate results resolve at shallower layers freeing deeper layers for subsequent reasoning.

problem: Benign overfitting in leaky ReLU networks was established only for gradient flow; directional convergence in discrete gradient descent under general mixture data remains unproven.
approach: Establishes directional convergence of network parameters and classification error bounds for fixed-width leaky ReLU two-layer classifiers trained on mixture data via gradient descent.
contribution: Proves benign overfitting occurs on mixture data setting broader than prior nearly-orthogonal settings; identifies phase transition and characterizes cases where benign overfitting provably fails despite directional convergence.
